name: When Sport Became History
description: Cricket grounds, boxing rings, football pitches and a few Olympic arenas where a match carried the weight of politics, race and nations, from Bodyline to Qatar.

checkpoints.name: Rules and rivalries
checkpoints.note: The Football Association wrote down common rules for football in 1863, and from 1882 the Ashes made cricket between England and Australia a contest of national pride. The Brooklyn Dodgers became the team of a whole borough.

checkpoints.name: Sport under dictators and after
checkpoints.note: Bodyline made the Ashes bitter and Don Bradman's batting was its target. Italy's fascist regime staged and won the 1934 World Cup, the 1936 Berlin Olympics put the Nazi state on show, the racehorse Seabiscuit cheered Depression America, and Jackie Robinson joined the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1947, breaking baseball's colour line.

checkpoints.name: New heroes
checkpoints.note: Brazil built the Maracana for the 1950 World Cup, and Uruguay beat the hosts there. West Germany's win in 1954 lifted a defeated nation, Pele became football's first global star, and in 1968 athletes used the Mexico City Olympic podium to protest against racism.

checkpoints.name: Spectacle and rivalry
checkpoints.note: Attackers killed members of the Israeli team at the 1972 Olympics. Title IX opened American school sport to women, Billie Jean King won the Battle of the Sexes, Martina Navratilova left Czechoslovakia to play in the West, and Muhammad Ali fought the Rumble in the Jungle and the Thrilla in Manila, while apartheid South Africa was shut out of world sport.

checkpoints.name: Nations and icons
checkpoints.note: Maradona took Argentina to the 1986 World Cup title, and the Hillsborough disaster of 1989 changed how football grounds were built. In 1995 South Africa won the Rugby World Cup it hosted, and Nelson Mandela used it to unite the country. A Women's World Cup began in 1991, Africa hosted the men's in 2010, and Qatar's in 2022 drew protest over migrant workers.
